confidence_notes: I based the food, coffee and beer anchors on web searches of cost-of-living aggregators: Numbeo, Wise, Citycost, Stamped Nomad and nomad.watch. They broadly agreed on an inexpensive meal of about 100 THB (about $3), a cappuccino of about 97 THB ($2-2.50), a domestic draft of about 80 THB rising to around $2.30-3 at beach bars, and a mid-range meal for two of about 1,175 THB (about $26-36). Several of these sources warn about small samples, and Numbeo's data was last updated in April 2025. I nudged the figures up slightly to reflect beach-strip tourist pricing. My one search for cocktail and wine prices found no usable aggregated figures for Koh Lanta. I estimated those two anchors from beer, at about 2.5x the beer price, which fits typical Thai island beach-bar pricing. Wine in Thailand is heavily taxed, so the wine-by-the-glass figure is especially uncertain. The four accommodation anchors are holistic estimates from general knowledge, not from searches or listings. They assume July's rainy low season, when rates are discounted and some properties close, so they could be noticeably higher in high season.
comparable_city_reasoning: The anchors are based on Koh Lanta-specific aggregator data, cross-checked against other Andaman-coast Thai island and beach destinations (Ao Nang/Krabi, Koh Phi Phi and Phuket's quieter beaches). Koh Lanta is generally a little cheaper than Phuket and Phi Phi, and about the same as Ao Nang.
